newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Sugar seen driving Tongaat H1 shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Sugar seen driving Tongaat H1 shr.

text.p: The Tongaat-Hulett Group Ltd was likely to post strong interim results boosted by a bumper sugar crop due to good summer rains and improved profits from property holdings, analysts said on Friday.
"The results will be driven mainly by sugar, after the recovery from drought. Improved property profits will also boost results," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings for the half year ended September 30 edging up to between 176.2 and 185.0 cents per share, with consensus at 179.7 cents. This compared to 150.6 cents per share previously.
The dividend was forecast at between 46.8 and 49.0 with consensus at 47.6 cents, compared to 40 cents per share.
Tongaat-Hulett is due to announce results on Wednesday.
Analysts said the aluminium business was difficult to call mainly as it was cyclical, but most said the business would post good results.
"It is difficult to predict but it will continue to do moderately well. It can be a cyclical business," one said.

Tongaat-Hulett revised up its sugar production forecasts in July for the 1996/97 season to 940,000 tonnes from 920,000 tonnes. It said production would be up a record 63 percent from last season reflecting good summer rains.
